sets.context:
Five friends - P, Q, R, S and T - sit in a row of five chairs numbered 1 to 5 from left to right, one person per chair, subject to these conditions:
1. R sits in chair 3.
2. P sits in chair 1 or chair 5.
3. Q sits immediately to the right of S.
4. T sits in chair 2 or chair 4.
5. P sits somewhere to the left of Q.

explanations: Correct. Condition 1 fixes R in chair 3, the middle position.
Incorrect. P is pinned to an end (condition 2), so P cannot be middle.
Incorrect. T is pinned to chair 2 or 4 (condition 4), so T cannot be middle.
Incorrect. Q must sit right of S (condition 3) with R fixed at 3, which forces Q to chair 5.
questions.prompt: Who sits in the middle chair (chair 3)?
questions.solution: 1. Condition 1 directly fixes R in chair 3. 2. Cross-check: P at an end, T at 2/4, S-Q adjacent with Q right of S and P left of Q forces P=1, T=2, S=4, Q=5 - consistent with R at 3. Answer A.

explanations: Incorrect. S sits in chair 4, two places to the right of T - not immediately beside T.
Correct. T is in chair 2 and R in chair 3, so R is immediately to T's right.
Incorrect. Q is the rightmost person (chair 5), three places from T.
Incorrect. P is the leftmost person (chair 1), immediately to T's LEFT, not right.
questions.prompt: Who sits immediately to the right of T?
questions.solution: 1. The full order is P(1)-T(2)-R(3)-S(4)-Q(5). 2. Immediately right of chair 2 is chair 3. 3. Chair 3 holds R. Answer B.

explanations: Incorrect. P and T occupy chairs 1 and 2 - adjacent, not the two ends.
Incorrect. S and Q occupy chairs 4 and 5 - adjacent, not the two ends.
Correct. Chair 1 holds P and chair 5 holds Q.
Incorrect. T and R occupy chairs 2 and 3 - the middle block.
questions.prompt: Which pair occupies the two end chairs (1 and 5)?
questions.solution: 1. P must take an end (condition 2) and sit left of Q (condition 5); Q must sit right of S (condition 3). 2. The only consistent placement is P=1 with Q=5 (S=4, T=2, R=3). 3. Ends are P and Q. Answer C.

explanations: Incorrect. After the swap T sits in chair 4, which is immediately to R's RIGHT, not left.
Correct. After S and T interchange, the order is P-S-R-T-Q, so chair 2 (left of R) holds S.
Incorrect. P stays in chair 1, two places left of R.
Incorrect. Q stays in chair 5, at the far end.
questions.prompt: If S and T interchange their seats (everything else unchanged), who sits immediately to the left of R?
questions.solution: 1. Original order: P(1)-T(2)-R(3)-S(4)-Q(5). 2. After swapping S and T: P(1)-S(2)-R(3)-T(4)-Q(5). 3. Immediately left of chair 3 is chair 2, which now holds S. Answer B.

sets.context:
A 3-member team is to be chosen from six people - A, B, C, D, E and F - subject to these conditions:
1. If A is chosen, B is also chosen.
2. C and D are never chosen together.
3. E and F are never chosen together.
4. If D is chosen, E is also chosen.
5. F is chosen.
6. C is not chosen.

explanations: Incorrect. D needs E (condition 4), but E is barred by F (condition 3), so D is out.
Incorrect. E is barred outright by F's presence (condition 3).
Correct. F is fixed; C is out (6); E is out with F (3); D is out without E (4) - leaving exactly A and B to fill the two remaining slots.
Incorrect. C is explicitly excluded by condition 6.
questions.prompt: Which of the following must be true of the team?
questions.solution: 1. F occupies one slot (5); C is out (6). 2. E cannot join F (3), so E is out. 3. D needs E (4), so D is out too. 4. Two slots remain and only A, B are eligible - both are in (A needs B per condition 1, satisfied). 5. The team is exactly A, B, F; A is chosen. Answer C.

explanations: Incorrect. 3 counts (A,B,F) plus invented teams that violate conditions 1-4.
Correct. With F required and C allowed, the valid teams are (A,B,F) and (B,C,F) - exactly two.
Incorrect. 1 counts only the original team, forgetting (B,C,F) becomes legal once C is allowed.
Incorrect. 6 counts every team satisfying conditions 1-4, forgetting F is still required.
questions.prompt: If condition 6 is dropped (C may now be chosen) while all other conditions stay, how many different valid teams are possible?
questions.solution: 1. F is still required. 2. Candidate teams with F satisfying conditions 1-4: (A,B,F) checks out; (B,C,F) checks out (B needs nothing; C,D fine; E,F fine). 3. (A,C,F)? A needs B - absent, invalid. (C,D,F)? C,D together - invalid. (D,E,F)? E,F together - invalid. 4. Exactly two. Answer B.

explanations: Incorrect. C appears in only one of the three possible teams ((B,C,E)).
Incorrect. D appears in only one of the three ((B,D,E)).
Correct. The valid teams are (A,B,E), (B,C,E), (B,D,E) - B is in all three.
Incorrect. F is excluded by the new condition (E and F never go together).
questions.prompt: Suppose conditions 5 and 6 are replaced with a single new condition: E is chosen (conditions 1-4 stay). Who is definitely on the team?
questions.solution: 1. E is fixed; F is out (condition 3). 2. Enumerate triples with E, no F, satisfying 1, 2, 4: (A,B,E) valid; (B,C,E) valid; (B,D,E) valid (D needs E, present). 3. (A,C,E)? A needs B - invalid. (C,D,E)? C,D together - invalid. (A,D,E)? A needs B - invalid. 4. B is in all three valid teams. Answer C.

explanations: Incorrect. (B,C,F) violates condition 6 - C is excluded.
Correct. A needs B (present), C,D and E,F pairs absent, F present, C absent - all six conditions satisfied.
Incorrect. (B,D,E) has no F, violating condition 5.
Incorrect. (A,C,E) violates three conditions at once: no B for A, C present, no F.
questions.prompt: Which of the following is a valid team under all six original conditions?
questions.solution: 1. Test each against conditions 1-6. 2. (B,C,F): fails condition 6. 3. (B,D,E): fails condition 5. 4. (A,C,E): fails 1, 5 and 6. 5. (A,B,F): A has B; C,D and E,F pairs absent; D absent so 4 is vacuous; F present; C absent - valid. Answer B.
